context_requirements: Expression of SLC6A4 (SERT) or other monoamine transporters for transporter-mediated uptake
Functional 5-HT signaling or intracellular serotonin stores
Sufficient exposure time (24 h) for secondary transcriptional changes; 6 h is likely too early
Presence of apoptotic machinery (BAX, caspase-3) for pro-apoptotic effects
falsifiers: No change in any landmark gene at 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Strong, consistent upregulation of proliferation markers (e.g., MYC, CCND1, MKI67) at 24 h
Clear transcriptional response at 6 h with magnitude strong, contradicting slow kinetics
No evidence of apoptosis or stress-response gene induction at 24 h despite reported pro-apoptotic effects

evidence.supports: SERT acts as tumor suppressor; fluoxetine abolishes SERT-5-HT pro-apoptotic effects via STAT3 inhibition
Chronic fluoxetine alters mitochondrial and plasticity transcriptomic pathways in neurons
Fluvoxamine reduces apoptosis in influenza-infected lung epithelial cells
Fluoxetine has minimal in vitro effects on sarcoma proliferation but modulates tumor microenvironment in vivo

changes: No direction changes were required: the late_up and late_down lists are consistent with SSRI-induced stress/autophagy/AP-1 and anti-proliferative signatures, and no gene appears in both lists.
No specificity changes were required: the proximal lists are empty, so no generic proliferation or stress genes are placed in proximal lists.
No line-response changes were required: all nine lines are assigned weak or none, consistent with the low-confidence, transporter-dependent, cell-context-dependent mechanism.
No kinetics or magnitude changes were required: slow kinetics with no 6 h response and weak 24 h response is consistent with the cited evidence.
No evidence changes were required: all four cited abstracts support the stated claims.
